quizzes.title: Christianity quiz
quizzes.blurb: Ten questions on the Gospels, the apostles and the early church.

questions.q: In which town was Jesus born, according to Matthew and Luke?
questions.why: Matthew and Luke place his birth in Bethlehem of Judea; he grew up in Nazareth.

questions.q: Who baptised Jesus in the Jordan?
questions.why: John the Baptist baptised him, and the Gospels say the Spirit descended like a dove.

questions.q: Which disciple denied knowing Jesus three times?
questions.why: Peter denied him three times before the rooster crowed, as Jesus had said he would.

questions.q: Which Gospel opens with "In the beginning was the Word"?
questions.why: John's Gospel opens by echoing Genesis 1:1.

questions.q: On the road to which city was Paul converted?
questions.why: A light from heaven struck him down on the road to Damascus.

questions.q: Which Roman governor sentenced Jesus to be crucified?
questions.why: Caiaphas was the high priest; Pilate gave the order.

questions.q: What did Jesus turn water into at the wedding in Cana?
questions.why: John calls it the first of his signs.

questions.q: How many apostles did Jesus choose as "the Twelve"?
questions.why: Twelve, matching the twelve tribes of Israel. Luke also mentions a wider group of seventy.

questions.q: Which commandment did Jesus call the greatest?
options: Love God with all your heart
questions.why: He quoted Deuteronomy 6:5, and gave "love your neighbour as yourself" (Leviticus 19:18) as the second.

questions.q: Where was the creed that calls Jesus "true God from true God" first written, in AD 325?
questions.why: The Council of Nicaea in 325; the creed was expanded at Constantinople in 381.

quizzes.title: Islam quiz
quizzes.blurb: Ten questions on the Quran, the Prophet and Islamic practice.

questions.q: What is the first surah of the Quran?
questions.why: Al-Fatihah, "the Opening", is recited in every unit of the daily prayer.

questions.q: Which angel brought the revelation to Muhammad?
questions.why: The Quran names Gabriel as the one who brought it down to the Prophet's heart.

questions.q: Which woman is the only one named in the Quran?
questions.why: Mary is named 34 times, and surah 19 carries her name. Eve is never named in the Quran.

questions.q: In which month was the Quran first sent down?
questions.why: "The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Quran."

questions.q: What is the longest surah?
questions.why: Al-Baqarah, with 286 verses; it contains the Throne Verse (2:255).

questions.q: Which surah does not begin with "In the name of God, the Merciful"?
questions.why: At-Tawbah (surah 9) is the only one without the basmala.

questions.q: How many daily prayers were finally made obligatory on the Night Journey?
questions.why: The hadith says fifty were first commanded and reduced to five after Moses urged Muhammad to ask for less.

questions.q: What is Muhammad's migration from Mecca to Medina in 622 called?
questions.why: The Hijra; the Islamic calendar counts its years from it.

questions.q: What does the Quran call Jesus, in Arabic?
questions.why: "His name is the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary." The Quran denies that he is the Son of God (9:30).

questions.q: Which surah is a one-line statement that God is One, neither begetting nor begotten?
questions.why: Al-Ikhlas, "Sincerity": a short creed that many read as an answer to the Trinity.

quizzes.title: Judaism quiz
quizzes.blurb: Ten questions on the Torah, the festivals and the rabbis.

questions.q: How many books are in the Torah?
questions.why: Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy: the five books of Moses.

questions.q: How does the Shema begin?
questions.why: "Hear, O Israel: the LORD is our God, the LORD is one." It is said morning and night.

questions.q: What is the Day of Atonement called?
questions.why: Yom Kippur, a day of fasting and repentance.

questions.q: Which festival remembers the Exodus from Egypt?
questions.why: Passover, with the seder meal and unleavened bread.

questions.q: When does the Sabbath begin?
questions.why: Jewish days begin at evening ("there was evening and there was morning", Genesis 1:5), so the Sabbath runs from Friday sunset to Saturday night.

questions.q: How many commandments do the rabbis count in the Torah?
questions.why: 613: 248 positive commands and 365 prohibitions.

questions.q: The Talmud is made up of the Mishnah and the...
questions.why: The Gemara is the rabbis' long discussion of the Mishnah.

questions.q: Which king built the first Temple in Jerusalem?
questions.why: David planned it; Solomon built it.

questions.q: Which book of the Hebrew Bible never mentions God by name?
questions.why: Esther; it is read at Purim.

questions.q: Who is called God's "friend" in the Hebrew Bible?
questions.why: "Abraham my friend". The New Testament (James 2:23) and the Quran (4:125) say the same.

quizzes.title: Which book says this?
quizzes.blurb: Bible, Quran or Torah? Guess where each line comes from. Some will surprise you.

questions.q: "Love your neighbour as yourself."
questions.why: Jesus was quoting the Torah: it is Leviticus 19:18.

questions.q: "There is no compulsion in religion."
questions.why: Quran 2:256.

questions.q: "An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth."
questions.why: Exodus 21:24. Jesus quotes it to set it aside (Matthew 5:38-39), and the Quran says it was written for the Jews (5:45).

questions.q: "Whoever kills a soul, it is as if he had killed all mankind."
questions.why: Quran 5:32, which says it was decreed for the Children of Israel. The Mishnah has almost the same words (Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5).

questions.q: "God is love."
questions.why: 1 John 4:8.

questions.q: "Their blood is on their own heads" for a man and woman caught in adultery, who are put to death.
questions.why: Leviticus 20:10 sets death for adultery. The Quran's punishment is a hundred lashes (24:2); stoning comes from hadith.

questions.q: "I did not come to bring peace, but a sword."
questions.why: Jesus, in Matthew 10:34.

questions.q: "Say: He is God, the One. God, the Eternal."
questions.why: Quran 112, Al-Ikhlas.

facts.t: Mary is named 34 times in the Quran, more than in the whole New Testament, and has a surah named after her.
"Love your neighbour as yourself" is from the Torah. Jesus was quoting Leviticus.
Quran 5:32, "whoever kills a soul... as if he had killed all mankind", is almost word for word in the Mishnah.
The Quran calls Jesus al-Masih, "the Messiah", while denying that he is the Son of God.
The word "Trinity" never appears in the Bible. The doctrine was defined at the councils of 325 and 381.
Moses is named in the Quran more than any other prophet, more than 130 times.
The Book of Esther never mentions God, yet it is in the Hebrew Bible and the Christian Old Testament.
All three faiths call Abraham God's friend: Isaiah, the letter of James, and the Quran.
Both the Torah and the Quran forbid pork. Most Christians eat it, citing Peter's vision and Mark 7.
The Quran says Jesus spoke as a baby in the cradle, a miracle the Gospels do not record.
The Quran's story of Jesus making clay birds come alive is also found in the second-century Infancy Gospel of Thomas.
The rabbis count 613 commandments in the Torah: 248 to do and 365 not to do.
